title: Proper scheme curves define objects of the curve stack
statement: Let k and Omega be fields [def-weil-field], a:Spec Omega -> Spec k a morphism, C a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and f:C -> Spec Omega a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] with topological Krull dimension at most one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. There is a ProperCurveFamily X over a [def-sfb-proper-curve-moduli] whose algebraic-space presheaf over Spec k is isomorphic to h_C, and this isomorphism identifies the projection of X with h_f. No reducedness, connectedness or nonemptiness is assumed.

proof.text: Take the representable fppf sheaf of C over Spec k, with projection yoneda of f. The representable sheaf is an algebraic space: its diagonal is represented by scheme fibre products and it has the identity etale atlas. The morphism to Spec Omega is flat over a field. Properness supplies separatedness, quasi-compactness, local finite type and universal closedness. A finite-type scheme over a field is locally finitely presented and a separated morphism has quasi-compact diagonal. These properties survive etale charts and arbitrary scheme base change.

For any algebraically closed field extension of Omega, the geometric fibre is the corresponding base change of C. Dimension of this finite-type scheme does not increase under a field extension. On a represented presheaf its field-point topology agrees with the scheme topology. Hence every fibre has dimension at most one, giving the final field of IsProperCurveFamily. Assemble the structure with the represented presheaf; the identity comparison gives the required projection equation.

theorem ProperCurveModuli.exists_scheme_family {k Ω : Type u} [Field k] [Field Ω]
    (a : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (C : Scheme.{u})
    (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of Ω)) (hf : IsProper f) (hdim : topologicalKrullDim C ≤ 1) :
    ∃ X : ProperCurveFamily (Over.mk a),
      ∃ e : X.space.obj.obj ≅ yoneda.obj (Over.mk (f ≫ a)),
        e.hom ≫ yoneda.map
          (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk (f ≫ a)) (V := Over.mk a) f rfl) = X.projection
